Application 9.4.1 requires DB 9.11.1 (minimum and target), upgraded from 9.11.0. Text-only migration seeds 23 language keys, fills missing/blank translations and exact English fallbacks in non-English locales, preserving other authored copy. At each article UI permission's first creation, users/guests keep Details and lose Images, Attachments, Related rows, Task progress and Edit/Edit language versions/Delete until granted; later grants/revocations persist. Anonymous visitors receive their guest group's UI grants. Home keeps its full site name, phone layout and sharp 128 px site icons. Home article buttons are server-side, configured through the administrator API; Home rendering follows in a later release.

Application 9.4.2 requires DB 9.11.2 (minimum and target), upgraded from 9.11.1. Text-only migration seeds article-view explanations and group field-setting warnings in Finnish, English, Chinese and Cantonese, filling only missing/blank translations; no right is granted or removed. Missing article-view rights remove clickable styling and explain attempted openings; group view settings warn and live updates stop retrying after 401/403. Administrators choose Home article buttons below text or as top-row pills; the open menu keeps its button. Optional operator Home at / stays off until data/storage/site_root/index.html exists and the Home switch is on; login_to_browse still decides access. Pages, favicon and shared-link previews use site identity and Home slogan fallbacks. Hidden source columns hide generated name filters. Lazy modules preload from /frontend/dist/. Runner images require its configured upload directory, identical to the web server's; no directory refuses images while text works. Readiness requires ChatGPT subscription sign-in; API-key logins remain unavailable. Image-first panels gain rounded corners and responsive spacing; the photo rounds after scrolling. Product view names survive startup; the development layout lock appears only in Cards and Article.

Application 9.4.3 keeps DB 9.11.2 unchanged (minimum and target); upgrading from 9.4.2 needs no database step, migration or database release record. Opening an article from cards styles newly bound surfaces without repainting every card, preserving appearance, previews and themes. Development desktop measurements on 60 rows: CSS writes 52,307 to 866, longest main-thread task about 290 ms to 120 ms, click to visible article about 470 ms to 250 ms; these are not production timing guarantees. Large datasets gain most: fintravel.fi's reported 6.5-second freeze came from repaint work growing with the square of visible cards. Administrators' Workline observatory has one desktop content scrollbar instead of two; phone/tablet scrolling at 900 px and below is unchanged. A shared article-presentation contract has no visible effect or new presentation; operators can optionally export saved settings and their current resolution as deterministic JSON from a read-only database-copy snapshot that always rolls back, without changing settings or rights. Developer tooling accepts explicit Claude worker effort; a browser-test locator was corrected.

Application 9.5.0 upgrades database 9.11.2 to 9.12.0 on first start; minimum and target are 9.12.0. The 21 migrations preserve and materialize article settings and audiences in ordered per-presentation bundles with an atomic combined-editor save, add per-image-use card presentation and focal points, extend filter bar preferences, associate object translations with read-rights ownership, add the three-line table-cell default (administrator range 1–30), seed reviewed interface wording while preserving site edits, make first-run suggestions read-only, add category heading order and record the database release last. New opener activation, Page layout and the image-presentation editor remain later work. Filter sections share stable layout, order and visibility choices; category matching is explained; administrators can save dataset default views; readable datasets offer text search independently of AI rights; integer-ID matches lead results. Home stays first and reachable, uses the matching side menu and offers optional Serif story text. Cards, tiles and articles share safe localized record names; rich-text links retain safe destinations and article arrows are centred. Image sourcing prefers decodable formats, retaining AVIF at lower priority. Read boundaries cover object names, linked labels, filter values, comments and row events; administrator tools, writes, registration and first-run setup are more tightly guarded. Every first-administrator submission requires the server-log setup code. Maintenance and payment reads no longer write; language-key retirement remains paused and scans require trustworthy evidence. Notices follow language and account rights. Native restore-check rehearses trusted authenticated packets in temporary databases without stopping the application; stored code still executes as superuser on the live cluster. Go 1.26.9, x/image 0.45.0 and x/text 0.43.0 fix HTTP, WebP and Unicode security issues. PostgreSQL/PostGIS image builds drop expiring pins. Test/tooling improvements and future-feature documentation add no further production capability. Article presentations share one Field settings editor: three projections and opening blocks in a five-column table, preserved group differences and scoped drafts, one atomic revision-checked Save verified by complete readback; phone tables scroll within the page and keep field identity visible.

Application 9.5.1 includes all eight commits on main after 9.5.0 and keeps database 9.12.0 unchanged (minimum and target); no migration runs and no database release record is added. Page image-first pilot: explicit row links and Home article buttons can show a contained whole image within the text column, or text alone without an image, using shared Back/Forward/close/Escape history. The Page pilot is opt-in: nothing changes until an administrator saves a Home article button with the Page view, or a direct ?view=image_first_page_view row link is used. It requires /ui/view/image_first_page_view in the catalogue's scope (currently tableless/global), plus the dataset's get-results right, including server row reads. Rollback: 9.5.0's strict reader rejects a stored Home article button view field and hides all Home article buttons. Before rolling back to 9.5.0, re-save the buttons without Page and remove the view field. Phone layout at ≤ 700 px: Home fills its stacked navigation row, sits beside the menu in the top bar, closes overlay menus, and the menu button has a complete border. Dataset headings have tighter spacing; the cover hero no longer adds the administrator's "hero extra height", as the owner asked for tighter phone spacing. Ordinary articles lose their frame and excess spacing; article/image-first record buttons become 44 px icons without thumbnails; all three article presentations stack detail names above values; revealed disabled image arrows dim and hidden arrows stay hidden. Tablet/desktop article layouts retain their behavior. At all sizes, disabled side-menu history buttons use the normal cursor. Home slogan: Serif story slogans up to 40 Unicode code points remain a title accent; longer slogans become a smaller italic lead below the title, outside the line reveal, with Finnish/English guidance. Documentation: appearance scope, resolution, drafts, permissions and storage are explained; merging guidance and proposed modularity checks change no shipped runtime behavior. Release tooling: read-only article BEFORE/AFTER reports, value-free owner difference lists and an offline SHA-256 gate bind approval to the exact differences and reject unapproved or missing differences without changing a database or starting the application.

Application 9.6.0 contains the 53 commits since 9.5.1 and upgrades database 9.12.0 to 9.13.0 on first start; minimum and target are both 9.13.0. Two migrations seed Finnish and English Home-search labels and status wording in both translation stores while preserving site-authored text, then record the database release. Before upgrading outside development (ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=dev), check that SESSION_SECRET_KEY (encryption) and SESSION_KEY (signing) have real values: an empty or example-placeholder value now stops startup before any database access. Preserve existing valid keys; installers generate fresh keys for new installs. Signed-in reads of protected storage require the full matching device and fingerprint browser binding; an unbound or partially bound signed-in request receives the anonymous answer. Public storage and caching are unaffected. Guests no longer receive browser-binding checks or security cookies; obsolete guest bindings are cleared, with functional session state retained. Every successful sign-in replaces its CSRF token; API clients must fetch a new one before writing and in-page login refreshes it. Unused post-login return state is removed. Sign-in and recovery share translated accessible code screens and email-code resend; one-time-code PIN entry avoids password-manager suggestions, with a revealable visual mask whose digits may be read aloud by screen readers. Home and dataset navigation render in the chosen language initially; the page remains behind its loading screen until that language is applied, capped at about 4.5 visible seconds once its assets can be shown, then reveals even without a startup-ready signal. Home uses a small sticky phone bar, readable-dataset site search with three matches per dataset and Back/close recovery, desktop grouped search without extra history entries, one-column boxes with small images and letter fallbacks, theme-aware edges, rounder boxes and consistent spacing. Thumbnails use dataset card image presentation and focal points, with stronger blur. Home text has logical alignment, a phone override and 12–18 px Serif story sizes (default 15); dark icons, media-shaped side navigation and rounded top tabs render correctly from the first view. Rapid Back/Forward and initial dataset history no longer cause load failures or duplicate steps. Rollback to 9.5.1 requires the 9.12.0 database backup, with subsequent database changes lost on restore. Before reusing 9.6.0 Home settings with 9.5.1, save story size 15 px and phone alignment As elsewhere to remove unsupported v5/v4 and store v3 or lower. Visibility saves immediately remove hidden/server-only fields from every cached view, cannot be undone by older metadata reads, and apply row-visibility gates after commit while preserving owner access. Unchanged language, tab-class and search writes preserve Observatory scroll and focus. Phone text search and selected filters align with shared tools; soft corners, expanding input-mode buttons, compact following category popups, rightmost panel controls and painted dark-theme bars improve dataset surfaces. Stacked cards and phone/tablet articles lose decorative photo frames while wide-card frames and special image rules remain; stacked detail lists have straight edges and Show more shares the category radius. Page-sized image-first articles have taller desktop images, consistent spacing and pause Home video while open. Site information reports build commit, dirty state and UTC build time. Check planning, opt-in report-only screenshot observations, installation fixture guards, browser cleanup/readiness/parallel checks and offline JSON tests improve verification. Removed unused styles add no visible behavior; embedded website listings remain future documentation.

Application 9.6.1 contains the 43 commits since 9.6.0 and upgrades database 9.13.0 to 9.13.4 on first start; minimum and target are both 9.13.4. Nine migration files implement four batches, each with a release record. DB 9.13.1 adds saved Home-box translated titles, category and sort queries, category-link limits, stable identities, multiple boxes per dataset and explicit inheritance, preserving existing boxes and intentionally empty lists; default boxes show three rows. DB 9.13.2 replaces exact automatic English sort-key defaults in Finnish and English and four exact legacy Finnish sort labels in both translation stores, preserving site-authored text, blanks and other languages. DB 9.13.3 adds the site-wide Home top-bar opt-in, off by default, with Finnish/English editor labels; replay preserves existing choices and nonblank translations. DB 9.13.4 adds the site-wide category-button width choice, defaulting to row-filling centred labels and preserving existing choices. Home leaves the top bar by default on every site but stays in the menu; administrators wanting it back must enable Show the Home button in the top bar on wide screens in Admin → Site settings → Home settings and save. It appears only above 700 px while Home is enabled. Rollback to 9.6.0 requires restoring the 9.13.0 database under a write freeze, losing subsequent database changes. The Home-box schema is DB 9.13.1; downgrading below it requires the pre-migration backup. The current Home editor leaves new box fields inert until the box editor ships; that is not a database downgrade. API-saved Home boxes obey visitors' read rules and omit unusable saved categories/sorts rather than broadening results, with administrator repair hints. Their reads, validation and connection/admission waits respect Home's remaining time budget. Home search overlays the site name on phones and at 701–1200 px, keeping focus on the trigger across breakpoints. Phone Home boxes use one full-width layer and 16 px text edges; Contact/article buttons fit and wrap labels with 54 px targets. Desktop boxes follow left/right text insets within an 800 px maximum. Trees retain explicit open/closed choices across reloads, keeping temporary reveals separate and discarding polluted legacy lists once. Guests see About when permitted, and release checks re-enable as soon as their wait ends. The site-wide category_filter_button_width_mode setting chooses fill_row_with_centered_label (default) or fit_to_label; empty badges take no space. Values open largest-count first, preserve administrator tie order and remain stable while open. Dataset hero tools gain a rule and decorative icons, exact default sort labels lose Sort without altering administrator edits, phone filter/reset controls share a row, and top-bar search becomes a button before truncating the dataset name and overlays it when opened. Table copying/navigation uses the selected row after infinite scrolling; grid copy excludes hidden fields and headers, preserves empty positions and treats whitespace as empty. Ctrl+C copies selected cells while preserving focused controls and native selections. Hidden/server-only geometry is excluded from map support in map views, API responses and intelligent search, and from geometry metadata, so maps cannot use that geometry for points. Generated linked-row labels become null for hidden, server-only or unregistered target display fields, including for guests; relation keys remain separate. Visibility saves refresh these projections immediately. Collection/vector sorting and filtering use only known readable columns: when the viewer cannot read the chosen sort column, results use a readable creation or ID column in the requested direction; semantic vector searches keep their similarity order, and withheld filters are ignored. Vector responses omit unreadable columns rather than failing the query; administrators and readers with all SELECT grants retain delivered fields and similarity order, independent of view field selections. Signed-in row saves tolerate failed, slow or empty provenance-name lookups, retaining the user id with unknown as the name. Startup stops adding duplicate registry-less foreign-key relations. New image uploads retain displayed dimensions; administrators can explicitly backfill old images through guarded batches at POST /api/admin/image-dimensions-backfill, defaulting to dry run, with unsupported structural galleries counted even without public namesakes. Stacked photos use stored dimensions from first paint within a 4:5 limit and 80% viewport height; unsized images remain square, and resizing keeps the fixed 300×300 wide frame. Article image controls share a 1200 ms idle timer and disabled arrows retain their theme skin at 28% opacity. Articles show one row-title heading, omit only an exact first content-heading match in the same known language and advise editors without changing stored text. Phone forms and dataset surfaces align on 16 px edges, with headings clear of the floating menu. Registration includes translated inline PIN errors in its server response. Profile verification and PIN/authenticator setup share translated labels, hints and inline errors; PIN setup adds an accessible reveal control. Only instances with FILTEREST_INSTANCE_INFO_FILE pointing to a record load the bottom-left badge, including on sign-in pages; it shows source and backup time, expands to commits/data source/refresh time in Europe/Helsinki and minimises to a dot. Production sites without the flag see nothing new and have no /api/instance-info endpoint. Native restore-check explicitly allows only pgcrypto and unaccent through repeatable --allow-extension or DATABASE_RECOVERY_ALLOW_EXTENSIONS; results/private evidence record opt-ins while default extension/language guards remain. Language-source scans batch changed/day-old evidence, preserve freshness and maintenance gates, lock in identity order and retry deadlocks up to three times. Successful scans writing at least 10,000 rows attempt VACUUM (ANALYZE) after releasing the scan lock, log totals/retries/durations/results and only warn on VACUUM failure. Browser tooling reduces identical project runs by default, with FILTEREST_E2E_MATRIX=full retaining six projects for weekends/site releases. Shared waits and readiness reporting, bounded permissions-test listing reads, phone-test exclusions, failed-run cleanup, slow-load waits and a corrected card test stub improve verification without adding runtime features.

Application 9.6.2 contains the 20 commits since 9.6.1 and upgrades database 9.13.4 to 9.13.5 on first start; minimum and target are both 9.13.5. The setting migration adds the site-wide boolean app_log_search_terms, off by default and preserving existing choices, and its release record records DB 9.13.5. Rollback to 9.6.1 requires the 9.13.4 database: restore the pre-upgrade backup under a write freeze, losing subsequent database changes. Before downgrading an application using Home's new No text below title style, select and save a supported style. Home can omit introductory text and longer slogans while retaining the Serif story heading and its short italic accent; stored text and reveal preferences remain, and shared-link descriptions use the cleaned description then the site name. Phone top bars use a 48 px edge-to-edge layout with menu, identity/search, search-toggle and dataset-panel cells; Home omits the panel cell. Articles show the translated dataset name. Square search fields have separate clear/submit controls and a hide toggle that retains text. Home retains its draft for the visit, offers clear when text exists and hides empty result boxes. Signed-in users see their own read-only login name on the account page. Sign-in dialogs stay open on backdrop clicks; other dialogs retain intentional backdrop dismissal and preserve drafts when text selection ends outside. Close buttons, Escape and assistive activation remain under the dialog's dismissal policy. The sign-in privacy-consent checkbox, gap and text form one clickable label; the notice link opens separately and consent stays required. Application logs exclude visitor search terms, request query strings/fragments, search-related database/provider error contents and malformed provider replies by default; AI search diagnostics that can repeat search words are suppressed, while search failures retain error class, SQLSTATE and diagnostic identity. Operators relying on search terms in logs can restore previous diagnostics by enabling app_log_search_terms in the system configuration settings view; changes take effect within five minutes, with missing/null/unreadable values and failed refreshes defaulting to off. Warm reads of other settings remain immediate, and older log lines are unchanged. Article view puts Previous/Next/Close above the title at every width; directions without neighbouring displayed results are disabled and image arrows still change that row's images. The view picker's Article split button remembers Article, Image-first article or Page-sized image-first article per dataset in this browser tab, including reloads; its keyboard/touch menu checks the current choice, choosing opens it, and Tab closes it with native focus traversal. Image-first choices fetch the open article's row afresh or the current listing's first row including search; an empty listing opens nothing and reports no results. Listing changes, any application address write, navigation away or newer choices cancel unfinished openings. A choice without permitted photos opens as text only, also after reload and Forward. Article/Image-first retain the Article right and Page its own; the picker keeps the phone filter panel open and later dialogs keep their normal dismissal. Back/Forward restorations complete their own hidden-field/category/view-fallback address repairs while newer navigation still cancels stale work and prevents late history replacement or dataset reselection. Table edits survive incoming changes without interruption or unintended saving; live refresh waits for editor closure and saved cells remain selected. Held multilingual changes preserve other languages, including initially empty fields and List view. Other rebuilds discard drafts without saving; ordinary reader refresh timing and shared searches remain. Concurrent-settings test isolation, phone sign-in/profile coverage, fixture timing/timeouts, sign-in/re-render helpers, temporary e2e naming and cleanup, the phone top-bar assertion, caller-search conventions and future browser-update planning are tests/documentation only and add no production feature.

Application 9.6.3 contains the six commits since 9.6.2 and keeps database 9.13.5 unchanged (minimum and target); no migration runs on first start when upgrading from 9.6.2 and no database release record is added. A rollback to 9.6.2 keeps the same database. Update checks: the checker, installer, updater and publisher share that tracked release source; the default source is unchanged. The checker follows at most one release API redirect within the HTTPS origin configured in its build, including GitHub Enterprise. Configure host, owner and repository in the tracked file before building; Enterprise uses that host’s /api/v3 API. Editing the file does not redirect an already built binary. A second redirect, a different origin, HTTP or user information in the redirect URL is refused. Failed checks report unavailable and retain any earlier successful result as historical only, without an update available marker; they do not prevent application operation or install updates. Keep redirects to one hop on the configured HTTPS origin, or correct the source and rebuild. Docker image builds: Docker images build again from this release’s source: the Go build stage includes the tracked repository identity needed to compile the binary. This matters for Docker installations and updates that build their image from source. Its binary embeds the same identity as a native build. The omission arose while introducing that file in this release; upgrading from 9.6.2 needs no additional operator step. Articles and cards: closing an article opened from a Home box returns to Home; closing one opened from a dataset list returns to that list. Browser Back and Forward restore the right row. Cards listed in the Article presentation use the same field frames, icons and grid as the selected standard or Glowy card style, keeping the Article presentation’s own field choices. Operators’ existing style selection also controls those cards’ appearance; their Article field choices are kept. Cards: the Glowy card's title and description icons, and in both card styles the title's dataset icon, stay at the top of their container when a title wraps or a description runs over several lines; a short one-line description stays centred next to its icon. The site setting Card description lines (card_description_lines), default 2 and range 1–12 in steps of one, now governs descriptions in both card styles, including descriptions shown with a field label that previously stayed at two lines whatever the setting. Longer descriptions are truncated; other field values keep their two-line preview. Release repository identity: release checks, installer downloads and publication tools read one tracked file, app/server_tools/repo_details.json; the repository itself is unchanged. The Go binary embeds the identity at build time, so editing the file does not redirect an already built binary. For updates, origin must have one fetch URL for that repository, matching the file’s host, owner and repository exactly: HTTPS with or without .git, or SCP-style and ssh:// Git SSH URLs as the git user with .git. FILTEREST_RELEASE_REPOSITORY must be unset, empty or exactly match the file's owner/repo value; conflicting origins or overrides are rejected before release evidence is fetched. Installer overrides follow the same rule. A missing, unreadable or invalid identity file stops setup before binary selection, including current or local binaries; correct the file or conflicting origin or override before retrying.

Application 9.6.4. Release date: 2026-11-11. Contains the two commits since 9.6.3. Database and rollback: The database moves from 9.13.5 to 9.13.6 on the first start of 9.6.4. The minimum and target are both 9.13.6. The database release comprises three SQL files: the row-opening presentation policy, localized controls, and one database release record. The controls let administrators set how rows open for the site or a dataset and let visitors return to the default. Existing nonblank translations are preserved. With no setting, rows open as before; existing dataset overrides are preserved and no site-wide backfill is needed. Before upgrading, keep a reviewed backup of the 9.13.5 database. A rollback to 9.6.3 requires restoring that database from the reviewed backup under a write freeze; database changes made after the backup will be lost. Returning to the earlier application also removes the new row-opening controls and restores its earlier opening behaviour. Field order: The field order saved in the field editor survives application startup and catalogue refreshes. Renaming a field keeps its place. New fields follow the saved fields in creation order, including in the add-row form. Dataset toolbar: The dataset toolbar stays stable between the original hero tabs and the listing's title and search. Menu and filter controls follow the visible toolbar in both states. Home and dataset navigation: Navigation buttons centre on the full toolbar when space permits, keeping at least 20 px clear of nearby edge controls. Home's side menu uses rectangular buttons and its top controls align with the Home toolbar. The sliding overlay keeps its edge while its outer shadow fades. Menu controls and environment badges have flat surfaces without shadows. Dataset loading: A rate-limited dataset-list request retries at most four times with growing delays. A server-requested wait is capped at 30 minutes and the waiting period survives a reload in the same tab. Recovery opens the requested view only while the visitor is still on that visit; it cannot replace a newer navigation. Related items: Articles with many incoming relations open their related items faster. Each child table's column query reads its foreign-key metadata once. Composite keys use their declared column pairs. When a field has several targets, related items prefer the shortest key, breaking ties by target table and column name. This can change which target appears where several relations share a field. Closing articles: Closing an article returns to the card list it was opened from, including after switching to another record from the article's list. Row-opening presentation: Administrators can choose Open rows as in the appearance palette under Article, for all datasets or one dataset: Article, Image-first article or Page-sized image-first article. An explicit link or history entry chooses the presentation for that opening. Otherwise the visitor's own choice for the dataset in this tab takes precedence, then the dataset override, then the site default. Removing a dataset override restores inheritance. Saving the same value as the site default pins it for that dataset, even if the site changes. The view picker's Use default removes the tab's preference. Reloading the same tab retains a choice only for the same verified user. Another account or a guest cannot inherit it. Verification uses existing startup responses, without another request; retained choices wait for identity confirmation. The dataset's listing view remains a separate setting. Clicking an ordinary card photo still opens the image viewer. Home article buttons without an explicit presentation now inherit these choices; explicitly configured Article or Page buttons keep their choice. Existing Article and Page permissions still apply, including to inherited Home buttons, row contents and media. Ordinary foreign-key links remain usable when a row presentation is unavailable. An image-first article without permitted photos opens as text only. Classic article openings keep their request guard while rebuilding the list and loading the article. Home, search and related-row links finish dataset navigation before opening the requested row, only while the original request is current and that dataset is selected. A newer request prevents the old article from opening. These handoffs cannot automatically open the first result instead; ordinary Article visits still open their first result. Closing an image-first article also leaves its image arrows usable on reopening. API clients that need the new appearance field must send X-Filterest-Appearance: row-presentation. Requests without it retain the previous appearance response shape and revision tokens. Updates to other appearance fields preserve the row-opening setting. Shared caches must honour Vary: X-Filterest-Appearance on these responses.

Application 9.6.5. Release date: 2026-11-11. Contains the one commit since 9.6.4. Database and rollback: The database is unchanged at 9.13.6, with the same minimum as 9.6.4. The minimum and target are both 9.13.6. No migration runs on the first start after upgrading from 9.6.4. Rolling back to 9.6.4 keeps the same database; no database restore is required for this application rollback. The selected photo's caption and credit described below no longer appear in Page-sized image-first articles after returning to 9.6.4. Selected photo credit: Page-sized image-first articles show the selected photo's localized caption and photographer link at the dataset's configured position, over or below the image. The position follows inherited site settings and live appearance changes. Both placements fit the displayed photo's width, including portraits narrower than the text column. A photo without caption or credit text leaves no empty caption box.

Application 9.6.6. Release date: 2026-11-12. Contains the two commits since 9.6.5. Database and rollback: The database is unchanged at 9.13.6, with the same minimum as 9.6.5. The minimum and target are both 9.13.6. No migration runs on the first start after upgrading from 9.6.5. Rolling back to 9.6.5 keeps the same database; no database restore is required for this application rollback. Returning to 9.6.5 removes the option to restrict the field selector to administrators, so guests and ordinary users see the selector again. Field-selector disclosure: A site can show the filter bar's Select visible fields section only to administrators. When enabled, guests and ordinary users do not see the section, including on the first render. Administrators retain the picker. Every visitor still receives the effective fields for the current dataset and view, even when the selector is hidden. The option is off by default. An authenticated user with the existing layout-save permission can enable it by sending only {"field_selector_admin_only":true} to POST /api/filterbar-section-layout/save, preserving other layout settings. The public GET /api/filterbar-section-layout reports the value. Sending false restores the usual selector for everyone. The selector stays hidden while the layout is unavailable. With the option on, it appears only after the field-set response confirms administrator rights. With an unrestricted layout, the local field picker remains available if the field-set request fails.
